title: First music jobs: speakeasy with the Hickman Brothers
summary: His first paid gig was a speakeasy job for 60 cents with the Hickman Brothers and others, then work out on the Lakefront with Kid Clayton.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: But what, for practicing or just playing? Practice. Well, in the meantime, while all this was going on, you were just playing music on the side? Yeah. And where did you play? Where was your practice?
My first job was at the UK Ball on the 7th. Made 60 cents.
60 cents, yeah. 60 cents. Who did you play with?
I played with the Hickman Brothers.
All right, and who else played?
John Bruce, Julius Simpson, Buddy Charles. And way around 1940 when I met Cheek at the Cotton Club.
Mm-hmm. And this first job, was it a dance or?
Oh, I see. And you just sat there and played? I sat there and played. Uh-huh. What did you make there? Just tips or did you get paid?
No tips, no, no tips. 60 cents what you made. Oh, for the long? Hot dog man was on the outside waiting for you to buy hot dogs. Out there. Out there.
How much should he charge you for the hot dog? 15 cents for hot dogs. Wow, it took a whole quarter of your night's pay.

And you needed two hot dogs to get full, so I got them with 30 cents. Oh, and then where did you play after that? Well, after that, I went out there by Mama Lou with Clayton. Oh. Out on Lakefront, Kit Clayton. And what year was that?
